new.x: Ashoka and Dasharatha dedicated the Barabar caves to the Ajivikas, the sect also patronised by Bindusara. Jainism is linked with Chandragupta and Samprati, and Buddhism with Ashoka's Lanka mission, but the Barabar dedications were to the Ajivikas; Vedic Brahmanas were not the recipients.

new.s: The Third Buddhist Council, after which Ashoka sent Buddhist missions to various regions, was held at
new.x: The Third Buddhist Council was held at Pataliputra under Ashoka, and missions such as Mahinda's to Sri Lanka and Mahadeva's to Mahishamandala followed. Rajagriha and Vaishali hosted the First and Second Councils, and Kashmir the Fourth under Kanishka.

new.x: The name Ashoka occurs in the Maski (Raichur, Karnataka) and Gujarra (Madhya Pradesh) minor rock edicts (APPSC-G1 2022). Girnar and Kalsi carry the 14 Major Rock Edicts, Dhauli and Jaugada the Separate Kalinga Edicts, and Delhi-Topra and Rummindei are pillar inscriptions, all using the title Devanampiya Piyadasi.

new.x: Ashoka was the first ruler to address his subjects and officials through inscriptions on rocks and polished pillars (APPSC-GS 2018). Chandragupta left no edicts, while Kharavela's Hathigumpha and Rudradaman's Junagadh inscriptions came later.
new.tq: First rock and pillar inscriptions to subjects = Ashoka (APPSC-GS 2018).
